heading.en: Interwar posts and corps command

body.zh-Hant: 一戰時他在法國隨步兵作戰。1940年他任本寧堡步兵學校校長，之後任步兵署長（1941–42年）。1942年他成立第三集團軍轄下的第十軍並任軍長，直到1943年2月接掌第三集團軍。
body.en: He served with the infantry in France in the First World War. In 1940 he was Commandant of the Infantry School at Fort Benning, then Chief of Infantry in 1941–42. In 1942 he activated X Corps as part of the Third Army and commanded it until he took over the Third Army in February 1943.

heading.zh-Hant: 第一集團軍：法國至亞琛與許特根森林
heading.en: First Army in France, Aachen and the Hürtgen Forest

body.zh-Hant: 1944年8月1日，霍奇斯接掌第一集團軍。他採納建議派第五軍解放巴黎，並下令部隊進城；他的集團軍突破亞琛南北兩側的西牆，參與攻占亞琛。為保護右翼，他須肅清許特根森林；官方戰史後來批評美軍忽略了魯爾河水壩。
body.en: After taking command of the 1st Army on 1 August 1944, Hodges sent V Corps to liberate Paris and ordered it into the city; his army broke through the West Wall north and south of Aachen and took part in the capture of the city. To secure his right flank he had to clear the Huertgen Forest; the official history later criticized the neglect of the Roer River dams.

heading.zh-Hant: 阿登反攻、渡萊茵河與戰後
heading.en: Ardennes, the Rhine and after the war

body.zh-Hant: 1944年12月16日，德軍發動阿登突襲；17日他請求投入作為盟軍最高統帥部預備隊的兩個空降師，20日他的集團軍與第九集團軍一併改歸蒙哥馬利的第21集團軍群指揮。此後他的部隊在雷馬根渡過萊茵河，1945年4月25日與蘇軍會師。他一直擔任第一集團軍司令，至1949年1月31日退役。
body.en: The German Ardennes offensive struck by surprise on 16 December 1944. On 17 December he asked for the two airborne divisions of the SHAEF Reserve to be committed, and on 20 December his army and the Ninth Army were placed under Montgomery’s 21 Army Group. His army later crossed the Rhine at Remagen and met the Soviets on 25 April 1945. He remained First Army commander until his retirement on 31 January 1949.

heading.en: The Trinity test and the atomic bombing campaign against Japan

body.zh-Hant: 1945 年 7 月 16 日，格羅夫斯在新墨西哥州親身觀看「三位一體」（Trinity）原子彈試驗。依能源部官方史料，他按「各人分處不同地點觀察、以防意外」的原則，離開奧本海默，與布希、康南特一同在基地營觀看。試驗成功後，格羅夫斯對奧本海默說「我為你感到驕傲」；當助手法雷爾說「戰爭結束了」，格羅夫斯回答「是的，在我們向日本投下兩顆炸彈之後」。對日原子彈攻擊（campaign）中，1945 年 8 月 10 日，廣島、長崎遭轟炸之後，格羅夫斯向陸軍部報告下一枚鈽彈可在八月中旬後備妥，並因名單上僅剩小倉兵工廠與新潟兩處目標而要求增列目標；杜魯門隨後下令立即停止原子攻擊。
body.en: On 16 July 1945 Groves observed the Trinity atomic test in New Mexico first-hand. Under his policy that observers be in different locations in case of an accident, he left Oppenheimer and joined Bush and Conant at base camp. After the success he told Oppenheimer he was proud of him, and when Farrell remarked that the war was over, Groves replied that it would be after two bombs were dropped on Japan. In the atomic bombing campaign against Japan, on 10 August 1945, after Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Groves reported to the War Department that the next bomb would be ready after about 17 or 18 August and, with only Kokura Arsenal and Niigata left on the target list, asked that additional targets be added; Truman then ordered an immediate halt to atomic attacks.

body.en: Doolittle was born in Alameda, California, in 1896, enlisted as a flying cadet in October 1917 and was commissioned a second lieutenant in the Signal Corps Aviation Section on 11 March 1918. He received a regular commission on 1 July 1920, made his first cross-country flight in September 1922, and later earned a master’s degree and doctorate at MIT.

heading.en: The Tokyo raid, 18 April 1942

body.zh-Hant: 1942年4月18日，16架B-25中型轟炸機從大黃蜂號航空母艦起飛，目標包括東京、名古屋、神戶與大阪。杜立德親駕第一架，上午8時20分起飛，中午12時25分抵東京投彈；所有16架都在中國降落或墜毀，或轉降蘇聯。他在中國期間被越級晉升為准將，並獲頒榮譽勳章。
body.en: On 18 April 1942, 16 B-25 bombers launched from the carrier Hornet to strike Tokyo, Nagoya, Kobe and Osaka. Doolittle took off at 8:20 a.m. in the first B-25 and dropped his bombs on Tokyo at 12:25 p.m.; all 16 aircraft reached China or crashed there, or diverted to the Soviet Union. He was promoted to brigadier general while still in China and received the Medal of Honor.
